hsr_doc: Map alignments for the high-speed corridors (texas/hsr.py CORRIDORS): waypoints (lat, lon) between each pair of neighbouring stations, drawn on the statewide map (tools/build_state_map.py, docs/map.html). For the map only: the model's track km stay texas/hsr.py's (straight line x TRACK_FACTOR); the map's note compares the two. A light effort. Texas Central (TC) follows its published corridor: south from the Dallas station along I-45, then the high-voltage transmission corridor through Ellis, Navarro, Freestone, Limestone, Leon, Madison and Grimes counties (the Brazos Valley station near Roans Prairie, SH 90) and Waller, into Houston along US 290 to the Northwest Mall site (FRA final EIS 2017 and record of decision 2020; Texas Central's county list). Dallas-Fort Worth (FW) follows NCTCOG's recommended alignment: the I-30 median, with a stop at Arlington's entertainment district (here a waypoint, not a modelled station) and a tunnel at the SH 360 / SH 161 interchanges (DFW High-Speed Transportation Connections Study, Phase 1, 2021; Phase 2 FAQs 2024-25). Every other corridor is drawn along the interstate or US highway it is named for, through the towns on it: no proposal exists to trace.
